doctrine: gnucobol-rs and KOBOLD prioritize migration-trust over compiler ambition: every byte, field, predicate, transformation, and audit artifact is admitted only through a sealed oracle court, while unsupported COBOL surfaces remain explicit evidence instead of inferred behavior.
oracle: GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 (cobc + libcob), built from pinned source; see reports/admission/RECEIPT-ADMISSION.md

readiness_levels.4: composed in the KOBOLD reconciliation corpus

courts.name: decimal MOVE
courts.proven: COMP-3/zoned/display field-storage bytes + cob_move result bytes
courts.not_proven: arithmetic; edited pictures; any other type pair
courts.breaks_claim: non-ASCII host; EBCDIC sign mode; locale != C.UTF-8
courts.lie_prevented: 'a MOVE result is close enough' — every byte of the receiving field is proven
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong MOVE result posted as a real value corrupts a record silently

courts.name: PIC field model
courts.proven: PIC+USAGE -> {type,digits,scale,flags,size} matching cobc
courts.not_proven: edited pictures; usages beyond DISPLAY/COMP-3
courts.breaks_claim: edited symbols; unsupported usage
courts.lie_prevented: 'a PIC width can be eyeballed' — the field model matches cobc's own attrs
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a mis-modeled field width mis-reads every downstream field in the record

courts.name: record layout
courts.proven: item byte offsets / group sizes / fixed OCCURS / REDEFINES(<=target) / FILLER matching cobc
courts.not_proven: SYNCHRONIZED; REDEFINES larger than target
courts.breaks_claim: alignment/SYNC; record-growth REDEFINES
courts.lie_prevented: 'offsets are obvious' — layout matches cobc's emitted offsets, not intuition
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong offset shifts an entire record, mis-attributing values to the wrong fields

courts.name: COPY expansion
courts.proven: COPY <name>. splice matching cobc -P text-word stream (nested, cycle-detected, provenance-mapped)
courts.not_proven: inline/multi-line COPY; OF/IN library; SUPPRESS
courts.breaks_claim: non-line-oriented COPY
courts.lie_prevented: 'substring replacement is close enough' — COPY REPLACING is whole-text-word
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong COPY expansion lays out the file against a copybook the data was never written with

courts.name: COPY ... REPLACING
courts.proven: whole-text-word pseudo-text replacement matching cobc -P (composes across nesting)
courts.not_proven: REPLACE directive; LEADING/TRAILING; identifier operands
courts.breaks_claim: substring replacement expectation; REPLACE directive
courts.lie_prevented: 'substring replacement is close enough' — REPLACING is whole-text-word
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong REPLACING substitution silently changes field identities across a whole estate

courts.name: arithmetic ADD/SUB/MUL
courts.proven: result bytes matching cob_add/cob_sub/cob_mul (cob_decimal path), truncate + nearest-away
courts.not_proven: DIVIDE; other rounding modes; ON SIZE ERROR; >38-digit bignum
courts.breaks_claim: >38 significant digits; float fields
courts.lie_prevented: 'rounding/sign are details' — receiving bytes match cob_add/sub/mul exactly
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong arithmetic result written back mis-states a balance or total

courts.name: VALUE initial image
courts.proven: 01 record initial WORKING-STORAGE bytes from VALUE matching cobc
courts.not_proven: VALUE under OCCURS/REDEFINES; non-fitting literals; no-VALUE records; figuratives beyond ZERO/SPACE
courts.breaks_claim: P-scaled parent; edited PIC
courts.lie_prevented: 'VALUE init is trivial' — the initial record bytes match cobc WORKING-STORAGE
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong VALUE image mis-seeds an uninitialized record read as real data

courts.name: PIC P-scaling
courts.proven: P scaling field model (digits/scale/size) matching cobc; trailing digits=9s+P scale=-P, leading digits=9s scale=9s+P
courts.not_proven: V+P; P at both ends; VALUE/MOVE on P field
courts.breaks_claim: V combined with P
courts.lie_prevented: 'P-scaling is just digits' — the asymmetric P digit/scale rule is exact
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong P-scale mis-places the decimal point, off-by-10x on money

courts.name: ODO physical-max layout
courts.proven: single trailing OCCURS DEPENDING ON physical maximum record size matching cobc allocation
courts.byte_domain: generated-C storage size b_REC[size] (NOT runtime LENGTH OF)
courts.not_proven: active/logical occurrence count; sliding; runtime validation; multiple/nested ODO
courts.breaks_claim: treating physical-max as logical length
courts.lie_prevented: 'LENGTH OF proves physical allocation' — ODO physical-max != logical length
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: treating ODO physical-max as the live length over/under-reads variable records

courts.name: LEVEL-88 eval
courts.proven: condition-name truth vs parent bytes matching cobc IF (alnum padded compare; numeric value compare; THRU inclusive)
courts.not_proven: SET; condition expressions; collating-sensitive ranges; Procedure Division execution
courts.breaks_claim: collating sequence; SET semantics
courts.lie_prevented: '88 truth is a string compare' — padded/numeric/THRU semantics are exact
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong LEVEL-88 truth mis-classifies account status (active/closed/delinquent)

courts.name: SET 88 TO TRUE
courts.proven: canonical parent bytes for SET condition TO TRUE (first VALUE / range lower bound) matching cobc; output satisfies eval_88
courts.not_proven: SET TO FALSE; FALSE clause; expressions; execution
courts.breaks_claim: SET FALSE expectation
courts.lie_prevented: 'SET TRUE writes anything satisfying the 88' — it writes cobc's canonical bytes
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong SET writes a status the program never intended

courts.name: packed ADD/SUBTRACT (cob_add_bcd)
courts.proven: ADD/SUBTRACT into a PACKED receiver, receiving-field bytes matching libcob cob_add_bcd
courts.not_proven: DIVIDE; SIZE ERROR; other rounding modes; bignum; float
courts.breaks_claim: >38 digits; SIZE ERROR control flow
courts.lie_prevented: 'packed add rounds like display' — cob_add_bcd keeps -0 on truncation
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong packed sign/rounding flips the sign of money on truncation

courts.name: fixed-record reconciliation
courts.proven: end-to-end decode of fixed-record data -> byte-stable JSONL + audit receipt + explicit unsupported, over sealed courts only
courts.byte_domain: JSON bytes + audit-receipt bytes (composing field/record/text-word/predicate domains)
courts.oracle: the sealed GNURUST courts (no new oracle)
courts.not_proven: transformed-record write-back; EBCDIC; edited PIC; line-sequential containers
courts.breaks_claim: treating KOBOLD output as business truth beyond sealed fields
courts.lie_prevented: 'decoded JSON is business truth' — it is record truth over sealed courts only
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: treating decoded JSON as business truth acts on record-truth as if it were account state

courts.name: binary storage (COMP/COMP-5/COMP-X)
courts.proven: binary field model + DISPLAY<->binary MOVE bytes matching cobc/cob_move
courts.fixtures: PIC sweep 416 (128 binary) + binary MOVE sweep 546 + 10M move-fuzz
courts.not_proven: binary arithmetic; SYNCHRONIZED; host-portable endian; COMP-6; float
courts.breaks_claim: big-endian host; SYNC alignment; binary arithmetic
courts.lie_prevented: 'binary is one rule' — COMP-X sizes tightly; IBM/MVS use 2-4-8, MF 1--8
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong binary width/endian mis-reads a key, branch, or amount on the wrong platform

courts.name: EBCDIC cp500 DISPLAY decode
courts.proven: raw EBCDIC alphanumeric DISPLAY bytes -> text under the admitted cp500 table
courts.byte_domain: raw EBCDIC field bytes -> decoded text
courts.fixtures: ebcdic sweep 256/256 (full byte range) + totality/bijection tests
courts.not_proven: cp037/other code pages; numeric EBCDIC zoned sign; national/DBCS; collation; binary/packed conversion
courts.breaks_claim: non-cp500 page; treating EBCDIC as record-wide convert-everything
courts.lie_prevented: 'EBCDIC conversion can be record-wide' — it is per-DISPLAY-field; binary/packed raw
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong EBCDIC decode silently garbles names, codes, and statuses

courts.name: edited-picture decode (16a+16b)
courts.proven: edited DISPLAY field bytes -> value + presentation text for Z 9 , . - + (16a) and $ * CR DB B 0 / (16b), slot-based
courts.byte_domain: edited DISPLAY field bytes -> value + text
courts.oracle: cobc MOVE numeric -> edited, DISPLAY edited bytes
courts.not_proven: numeric->edited formatting (16c); report writer; locale/currency; EBCDIC edited; edited arithmetic/VALUE
courts.breaks_claim: financial decorations; numeric->edited direction; edited under COMP/cp500
courts.lie_prevented: 'presentation string and numeric value are the same field truth' — they are separated
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: reading an edited presentation string as the numeric value double-counts or mis-totals

courts.name: binary fields in corpus
courts.proven: COMP/COMP-5/COMP-X binary fields decoded end-to-end in the reconciliation corpus (composes GNURUST.14)
courts.fixtures: 3 families x 120 incl binary fields, byte-stable
courts.not_proven: binary arithmetic; business truth
courts.breaks_claim: binary fields text-converted
courts.lie_prevented: 'binary fields are text under any encoding' — they are raw storage passthrough
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: reading a binary field as text under an encoding corrupts keys and amounts

courts.name: cp500 EBCDIC in corpus
courts.proven: cp500 alphanumeric DISPLAY decoded end-to-end with binary/packed passthrough proven untouched (composes GNURUST.15)
courts.not_proven: numeric DISPLAY under cp500 (EBCDIC zoned sign); business truth
courts.breaks_claim: EBCDIC conversion touching COMP bytes
courts.lie_prevented: 'EBCDIC touches all bytes' — binary/packed pass through untouched (proven)
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: converting binary/packed bytes as EBCDIC text destroys numeric values

courts.name: operator trust layer
courts.proven: explain-field (provenance/courts/value/non-claims), control totals, dirty-data evidence/strict, JSON key-collision refusal, stale-copybook risk in receipts
courts.not_proven: business truth; semantic validity; INITIALIZE/repair
courts.breaks_claim: coercing dirty bytes; silent key collision
courts.lie_prevented: 'a hand-written PASS table is evidence' — every value names its court + provenance
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: trusting a value with no provenance trail means an auditor cannot defend it

courts.name: cp500 EBCDIC zoned numeric decode
courts.proven: raw cp500 EBCDIC zoned-decimal numeric DISPLAY bytes -> value (cp500 translate + cob_get_sign_ebcdic overpunch sign)
courts.byte_domain: raw EBCDIC zoned field bytes -> value
courts.not_proven: cp037; edited numeric under cp500; binary/packed via this path; mixed/auto-detect encodings; national/DBCS
courts.breaks_claim: non-cp500 page; treating binary as EBCDIC zoned
courts.lie_prevented: 'EBCDIC numeric decodes like ASCII zoned' — the C/D/F sign zones differ
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a wrong zoned sign flips the sign of mainframe money

courts.name: COMP-6 unsigned packed storage + MOVE
courts.proven: COMP-6 field model (PACKED+NO_SIGN_NIBBLE, size ceil(n/2)) + DISPLAY<->COMP-6 MOVE bytes matching cobc/cob_move
courts.fixtures: pic sweep 432 (16 COMP-6) + comp6 MOVE sweep 98
courts.not_proven: signed COMP-6 (cobc converts to COMP-3); COMP-6 arithmetic; malformed bytes; dialect portability; pre-3.2
courts.breaks_claim: signed COMP-6; strict cobol85/2002 (reject it)
courts.lie_prevented: 'unsigned packed can reuse signed packed decoding with the sign nibble ignored' — COMP-6 size is ceil(n/2) (no sign byte) and signed COMP-6 is actually COMP-3
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: treating signed COMP-6 as COMP-6 (it is COMP-3) mis-reads the field entirely

courts.name: edited-picture decode composed
courts.proven: edited DISPLAY fields decode in the corpus; JSON keeps the presentation string, audit carries the GNURUST.16 numeric
courts.byte_domain: edited DISPLAY field bytes -> presentation + numeric
courts.not_proven: numeric->edited formatting; report writer; locale/currency; edited under EBCDIC
courts.breaks_claim: treating the presentation string as the numeric value
courts.lie_prevented: 'presentation string and numeric value are the same field truth' -- they are separated
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: replacing the edited presentation with its numeric (or vice versa) mis-reports money

courts.name: cp500 numeric DISPLAY composed
courts.proven: cp500 EBCDIC zoned numeric DISPLAY fields decode via GNURUST.17 in the corpus; audit names the court
courts.byte_domain: raw EBCDIC zoned field bytes -> value
courts.not_proven: cp037; edited-numeric under cp500; binary/packed via this path; mixed/auto-detect encoding
courts.breaks_claim: auto-detecting the code page; routing binary as EBCDIC zoned
courts.lie_prevented: 'EBCDIC numeric decodes like ASCII zoned' -- the C/D/F sign zones differ
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: auto-detecting the code page mis-decodes the whole EBCDIC file

courts.name: COMP-6 composed
courts.proven: unsigned COMP-6 fields decode via GNURUST.18 in the corpus; audit names the court; cp500 passthrough proven
courts.not_proven: signed COMP-6 (fails closed); COMP-6 arithmetic; malformed COMP-6 bytes; pre-3.2 behavior; dialect portability; EBCDIC conversion of COMP-6 bytes
courts.breaks_claim: treating signed COMP-6 as COMP-6 instead of COMP-3
courts.lie_prevented: 'unsigned packed can reuse signed packed decoding with the sign nibble ignored' -- COMP-6 has no sign nibble and signed COMP-6 is really COMP-3
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: treating signed COMP-6 as unsigned mis-reads it (GnuCOBOL makes it COMP-3)

courts.name: fixed-record container ingest
courts.proven: raw stream splits into fixed-length records with true offsets, named trailing/partial policies, byte-stable file audit, stable exit codes
courts.oracle: deterministic ingest invariants (not GnuCOBOL file I/O)
courts.not_proven: GnuCOBOL file organization; indexed/relative I/O; line-sequential runtime parity; auto-resynchronization; encoding auto-detection; silent repair of dirty bytes
courts.breaks_claim: silently absorbing a partial record or resyncing on a length mismatch
courts.lie_prevented: 'a fixed-record file just chunks cleanly' -- partial/trailing-newline shapes are policy decisions, not silent behavior
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: silently absorbing a partial/extra record drops or duplicates a banking record

courts.name: header/detail/trailer + declared control totals
courts.proven: variant routing by a declared discriminator (H/D/T) + declared-vs-observed control totals (count/debit/credit); balanced file reconciles, tampered trailer fails with a finding, unknown record type fails closed
courts.byte_domain: banking batch file -> per-variant records + control-total reconciliation
courts.fixtures: recon/banking H/D/T balanced + tampered; tests/banking.rs 3 green
courts.not_proven: posting truth; ledger truth; business truth; debit/credit polarity from a numeric sign; a balanced file being a correct file; a trailer match being ledger acceptance; auto-detected variants
courts.breaks_claim: inferring polarity from sign; treating a balanced file as accepted/correct
courts.lie_prevented: 'a balanced file is a correct, accepted posting' -- KOBOLD.BANK.1 proves declared==observed totals only, never posting/ledger/business truth
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: treating a balanced file as a correct, accepted posting moves money on an unverified batch

courts.name: declared accounting profile (numeric-role + debit/credit polarity)
courts.proven: debit/credit polarity from a declared source field + value tables only (never sign/CR-DB/name); only declared Amount-role fields are summed (identifiers/rates/codes never money); negative amount with declared D stays debit; unknown polarity fails closed
courts.byte_domain: declared accounting profile over banking detail records -> debit/credit totals
courts.fixtures: tests/banking.rs (5: balanced+rate-not-summed, tampered, negative-D-still-debit, unknown-fails-closed, credit-routing)
courts.not_proven: polarity from numeric sign; polarity from CR/DB presentation; numeric role from PIC or field name; transaction-code table unless declared; account-type/normal-balance polarity; reversal from negative sign; currency minor-unit correctness; posting/ledger/business truth
courts.breaks_claim: inferring polarity from sign/CR-DB/name; summing a rate or identifier as money
courts.lie_prevented: 'a numeric field is money and its sign is its posting side' -- ACCOUNTING.PROFILE.1 sums only declared Amount fields and takes polarity only from the declared source
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: summing a rate or account-id as money, or reading a sign as debit/credit, mis-states the ledger

courts.name: Db2 host-variable null/truncation indicator manifest
courts.proven: a decoded field is marked semantic_null / truncation_evidence ONLY via a declared S9(4) COMP-5 indicator pairing (negative=null, zero=present, positive=truncation); decoded bytes are always preserved; missing or wrong-usage indicator fails closed
courts.byte_domain: declared value/indicator pairing -> null/truncation state (bytes preserved)
courts.not_proven: SQL execution; Db2 precompiler transformation; SQLCA/SQLCODE interpretation; DBRM/package identity; the host value being the database value without its indicator; database truth
courts.breaks_claim: treating a cleanly-decoded value as present when the indicator says null
courts.lie_prevented: 'a cleanly decoded value is the database value' -- the DB2 null/truncation indicator can override it
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: acting on a decoded value the database marked NULL or truncated posts wrong or missing data

courts.name: DIVIDE receiving-field bytes
courts.proven: DIVIDE a BY b GIVING c + a INTO b GIVING c receiver bytes (DISPLAY/COMP-3, signed/scaled/narrowing, truncate + ROUNDED) matching cobc
courts.not_proven: divide-by-zero / ON SIZE ERROR; REMAINDER; COMPUTE / expression evaluation; procedure control flow; float; binary/edited receivers; other rounding modes; business correctness
courts.breaks_claim: divide-by-zero; COMPUTE; binary receiver
courts.lie_prevented: 'DIVIDE is ordinary decimal division and a mathematically correct quotient is enough' -- receiver scale, truncation toward zero, ROUNDED, sign-of-zero, and receiver bytes all matter
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: a divide result with wrong scale/rounding/truncation/sign/receiver-bytes misstates interest, fees, rates, allocations, or balances while looking plausible

courts.name: declared transformed-record reconciliation
courts.proven: a declared sealed transform (SET 88 TRUE / ADD / SUBTRACT) takes input bytes to output bytes; before+after decode + audit delta; byte-stable; undeclared transforms fail closed
courts.byte_domain: input record bytes -> declared-transform -> output record bytes + before/after decode
courts.oracle: composed sealed courts (GNURUST.12 SET-88-TRUE, GNURUST.7 ADD/SUBTRACT)
courts.fixtures: tests/recon2.rs (4: set+add compose, byte-stable, subtract, undeclared-fails-closed)
courts.not_proven: Procedure Division execution; production write-back; file rewrite parity; ledger acceptance; business truth; undeclared transforms; side effects beyond the declared field
courts.breaks_claim: treating a transformed record as written-back / accepted / business truth; applying an undeclared transform
courts.lie_prevented: 'a transformed record is a written-back, accepted, business-true record' -- RECON.2 proves only before/after bytes for a named sealed transform
courts.damage_if_overclaimed: treating transform evidence as a production write-back or ledger acceptance mutates or posts data that was never committed

transform_vs_read.note: Decode safety does not imply write-back safety; transformation courts are admitted separately.

note_lie_prevented: Each court names the specific future OVERCLAIM it prevents (lie_prevented). A proof is a defense against a particular lie, not a vague 'compatible'.
note_damage: Point #4 (mentorship): every positive claim names the ORGANIZATIONAL DAMAGE of overclaiming it. Negative capability is the product.
